ownership_reason: Only the gold walks the used slots and decides, slot by slot, between a BooleanAttribute (no value) and an Attribute with its value bound to the parent; hops 2-4 hand the two arrays, the count and the parent on unchanged and hop 1 only wraps the returned list read-only. The gold's javadoc promises the attributes of the used slots in slot order with a bare attribute, one without a value, listed as a BooleanAttribute; the slot 'empty' of <a normal="123" boolean empty=""> has the value "" and is not bare, yet the variant lists it as a BooleanAttribute. The decision of one slot leaks into the next inside the gold's own loop, so no one-line change of the arrays, the count or the parent above the gold restores it: the values reaching the gold are already right, a shorter count drops the slot, and copying or bounding the arrays changes nothing. The convention is pinned outside the gold: Attributes.iterator() and Attributes.html(Appendable, OutputSettings) treat slot i from keys[i] and vals[i] alone (html collapses a slot only through Attribute.shouldCollapseAttribute(key, val, out) on that slot's own value); Token.Tag.newAttribute(), which fills the slots, gives each attribute its own value (the pending value, "" for an empty value, null for none) and clears hasEmptyAttributeValue and hasPendingAttributeValue after every attribute; passing tests: ElementTest testAddBooleanAttribute (a bare slot is listed as a BooleanAttribute), TokeniserTest handleSuperLargeAttributeName (a valued slot is listed with its value), AttributeTest booleanAttributesAreEmptyStringValues (the iterator gives a bare slot its own empty value) and SelectorTest testByAttributeStarting (every key is listed).
